text:
Priya: Quick thread: how do we handle multi-tenant fairness when models have wildly different per-token costs? e.g., client A uses GPT-large-like model (cheap) vs client B using Llama-70B (expensive). Should quota be token-based only or cost-normalized?

Owen: Cost-normalized makes more sense for unit economics. We can represent quota as "cost credits" where each model has a cost-per-token metric and usage deducts cost*tokens.

Li: That affects admission heuristics: edges need to be aware of model_cost so they can decide whether a request would exceed budget. But model choice can be dynamic via routing.

ben-sre: Also need to ensure fairness invariants: we don't want clients gaming by switching to cheap models to circumvent limits if policy intended to limit real throughput. Maybe include policy tags: workload_class (e.g., interactive, batch) and cost_floor for certain SLAs.

Priya: Good point. Proposal: quotas are cost-credits by default. Policies can add constraints: min_cost_weight or per-model caps. Edges store lightweight model_cost map for common models; central provides updates.

Owen: For billing and audit, ledger entries should include model_id and cost_units charged. That helps reconcile billing vs fairness.

Li: Implementation note: cost-per-token varies by quantization and sequence-length due to batching effects. So central should publish effective cost estimates per model per profile, e.g., cost_per_gen_token and cost_per_prefill_token.

ben-sre: Danger: cost normalization adds complexity to fast path. Edge must keep costs small to decide. Suggest edges use per-model cost hints and central finalizes costs in adjustments. If divergence is detected, central issues compensating ADJUSTs via ledger.

Priya: We also need to handle model fallbacks: when routing migrates a request to a cheaper model, we must still apply the original model's expected cost if policy requires. Default behavior: charge based on actual model used unless policy_overrides.use_original_cost=true.

Owen: Telemetry: emit charged_cost, requested_model, routed_model, batch_size, and effective_cost_per_token. Important for audits.

Li: For Private deployments, model_costs might be customer-specific (different infra). So cost map must be pluggable and namespaced per deployment.

ops-bot: :information_source: Suggested metric - per_client_cost_rate_1m and cost_discrepancy_rate_5m. Alert if discrepancy > 0.5%.

Priya: Migration: introduce cost-credits shadow mode where we compute cost credits but don't enforce; measure divergence and adjust policies. After stable, flip to enforcement.

Owen: Edge API change: include model_id and hint tokens in admit proto so central can better estimate cost for admission.

Li: Security: model_id can leak info; for privacy, allow hashed model ids for Private deployments and a mapping in central if needed.

Priya: Decision: adopt cost-normalized quotas with per-model caps and policy override flags. Start with shadow mode for 2 weeks in canary. I'll add RFC details and examples.

ben-sre: I'll prepare runbook for cost-reconciliation spikes and throttling thresholds.

Priya: Thanks team, will follow up on RFC draft. :rocket:
